precepts.text: Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, and to seeds, as of many; but as of one: and to thy seed, which is Christ. Through that chosen lineage of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob came the twelve tribes and came Jesus the Christ. The law was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made. As soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with. The promise by faith of Jesus Christ is given to them that believe: it is not talking about everybody, it is the Israelites that believe on Christ that get the promises.
precepts.point: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above. If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is now what you do. But if you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you. All Israel is not Israel, as it says in Romans 9:6.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above.” If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is what you do. If you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you; all Israel is not Israel, as Romans 9:6 says. Galatians shows who it is for.

“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made.” Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and from that came the twelve tribes of Israel. “He saith not, And to seeds, as of many”: not to every nation, just that chosen lineage. “But as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.” Through that lineage came Jesus the Christ.

“Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made.” The promise was made to the twelve tribes of Israel. As soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with. “Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.”

“Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid.” If a law could have given life, righteousness would have been by the law. “But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.” That is not talking about everybody. From verse 16 it is the Israelites that believe on Christ who get the promises. There should be no confusion: those are the ones risen with Christ.

precepts.text: Is he the God of the Jews only? Is he not also of the Gentiles? Is he only for the southern kingdom? He is also the God of the northern kingdom: one God which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.
precepts.point: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above. If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is now what you do. But if you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you. All Israel is not Israel, as it says in Romans 9:6.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Galatians says “a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.” Romans explains it: “Is he the God of the Jews only?” Is he only for the southern kingdom? “Is he not also of the Gentiles?” Is he not also the God of the northern kingdom? “Yes, of the Gentiles also.”

“Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.” The circumcision is Judah, the southern kingdom; the uncircumcision is the northern kingdom. One God justifies both, by faith.

That is who Colossians 3:1 is speaking to: “If ye then be risen with Christ.” Both houses of Israel, Jew and Gentile, who believe on Christ are risen with him, and the promise by faith of Jesus Christ is given to them that believe.

precepts.text: James writes to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. Would it be a surprise for us to be called Greeks and barbarians? We were scattered abroad throughout the four corners of the earth.
precepts.point: Book read in class: Israel Redivivus, being a history of the tribes of Israel distinct from that of Judah, by Frederick Charles Danvers: with regard to the Israelites, it must be remembered that each tribe was divided into different families or subtribes, even as there were at a later date many tribes bearing different names who were collectively known to the Greeks as Scythians. The Scythians were nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. This is our book.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free.” A Christian will say, to hell with all the facts you just showed, because Greeks, Barbarians and Scythians are the other nations. Really, after reading all of that in context? No.

A history of the Jewish diaspora shows that the Jews in the western diaspora basically knew only Greek; their Torah reading and prayer were conducted in Greek, and the scripture was translated into Greek for those communities. So some of our people were called Greeks and some were called Jews, a language difference, but the same people. Barbarian comes from the Greek barbaros, what the early Greeks called all foreigners, including the Romans.

James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” Would it be a surprise for us to be called Greeks and barbarians? We were scattered abroad throughout the four corners of the earth, and Esau with his demonic self has tried to insert himself in our place.

Israel Redivivus by Frederick Charles Danvers says each tribe was divided into families and subtribes, and later many tribes bearing different names were known collectively to the Greeks as Scythians, the nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. Get mad; this is our book.

precepts.text: Strangers of Rome. We were the Romans too. Verse 5 already told you: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven. We were called Romans, we were called Greeks, we were called barbarians.

The Scythians were nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. This is our book.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Barbarian was the word the Greeks used for all foreigners, including the Romans. And we were the Romans too; that is what mainstream Christianity does not understand today. Acts 2 lists the people gathered at Pentecost: “Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes.”

Strangers of Rome. And verse 5 already said who they all were: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews, devout men, out of every nation.

So we were called Romans, we were called Greeks, we were called barbarians. When Colossians 3:11 says “neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian,” those are the names Israel carried in the places it was scattered, not the other nations.

precepts.why:
Colossians 3:11 ends, “but Christ is all, and in all.” Now they will say, see, Christ is in all. Then they go to Acts 10: “Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

Read the whole thing: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)” Lord of all what? Lord of all Israel, scattered in every nation.

And Paul clears it up himself in the very next verse of Colossians: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved.” Isaiah 45:4 says “Israel mine elect”; Leviticus 20:26 says the Lord has “severed you from other people”; Baruch calls Israel “his beloved.” He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathen. They know good and well this Bible does not belong to them, but in slavery they played on our ignorance. Now the God of Israel has poured His spirit on His people in these last days, and we know what the Bible is talking about.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In verse 11 Paul references us as the Greeks, the Barbarians and the Scythians. Then in verse 12 he says it one more time, plainly: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God”. He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathens to understand. Isaiah tells us who the elect of God is: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”.

Israel is his elect. So the elect of God that Paul is instructing in Colossians 3:12 are Israelites.

They know good and well this Bible don’t belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We couldn’t read or write; they taught it to us by oral tradition, wouldn’t let us read the Bible, and gave us the slave Bible where the majority of the Bible wasn’t even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about: Israel mine elect.

Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. He has severed us from other people, “that ye should be mine”: that ye, you Israelites, should be his people.

So right there in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it ain’t all nations. Just in case anyone was confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. The ones told to put on mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness and longsuffering are the holy people, the ones severed from the other nations to be his.

So the “holy and beloved” of Colossians 3:12 are the children of Israel: holy because he severed them from other people, beloved because he calls Israel his beloved.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh”. Going precept upon precept and in context, these servants would have to be Israelites, and these masters would have to be Israelites. It is a scripture they cherry-picked to fit their evil narrative. In The Religious Instruction of the Negroes in the United States they wrote of us, the 697,697 slaves of the 1790 census, as the original stock, in a state of absolute heathenism. They inserted themselves as the people and made us the heathens.

But the Lord did say this would happen: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. Moab and Seir look at the house of Judah and call us heathen.

How did we become like the heathen? By following after the heathen: celebrating their pagan rituals, Christmas, Thanksgiving; eating crab, shrimp, pork, lobster; praying to a white man. That is what makes us heathenistic. So the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israel, and the enemy calling Judah heathen is only what the Lord already said Moab and Seir would say.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Our enemies would like to think God cast us away because we became like the heathen, and that he isn't going to redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

The scripture foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us, and he would justify us through faith, through Christ. They may be mad all over again; it doesn't matter. We are still God's chosen people.

So the heathen Galatians speaks of justifying is Israel fallen into heathenism, the same servants Colossians 3:22 speaks to. That justification is only for one people, as Isaiah 45:25 shows.

precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

So it is what it is. Yes, we became heathen, following after the heathen in their holidays, their foods and their white image; but we are still going to be justified through Christ, and we shall glory. The justification is for one people, the seed of Israel.

That is why the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israelites and not the slave master's property to be taught his religion. The masters' books called us heathens in need of their instruction, but the Lord had already written that all the seed of Israel, heathen as we became, would be justified in him.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In 1673 Mr. Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions to masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves, a rubric to follow. In their evil minds they really believed they were masters. Did the Lord allow this to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. The first direction: remember that they have immortal souls and are equally capable of salvation with yourselves. That is where the false sense of equality comes from. It comes from slavery; it comes from Christianity.

Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

They believed they could be saved and then us; they are the people, and we come after. That is not how it goes. The same directions said that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God, and that is incorrect: we are not equal with these people. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, so the servants of Colossians and the salvation preached to them belong to Israel.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to make reconciliation for iniquity. Reconciliation means to do again: it cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God, and through Christ we get our reconciliation. And if the slave masters wrote that God was the reconciled father of their slaves, that means they knew who we are.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The slave masters' directions said that God is their reconciled tender father. God is our reconciled father, but that reconciliation is not for everybody. What does re mean? To do again: repeat, redo. Reconcile means to do it again. So if they wrote that reconciliation was for the slaves, that means they knew who we are.

Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God. Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

That is determined upon Daniel's people and holy city, and the most Holy anointed is Christ. Through Christ we get our reconciliation. So the very masters who twisted Colossians 3:22 wrote down, in their own directions, that their slaves were the people God reconciles: Israel.

precepts.text: Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things. We wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The third direction to the masters: serve your necessities by your slaves so as to prefer God's interest and their spiritual and everlasting happiness; teach them the way to heaven. So in want of all things we wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: even our religion had to come from the enemy we were serving.

The next page shows what that religion was for. They wrote that we were redeemed with them by Christ from the slavery of Satan and may live with them in the liberty of the saints in glory. They want us to go to heaven with them and live with them. That's called hell. That mind was beaten into us: a brother on the street asked if the Edomite could be saved, and said if he goes to hell, so will I, because he doesn't want to go anywhere without his master. That is the want of all things the curse brought, and why the master's reading of Colossians 3:22 still holds our people.

precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The masters' own book says of us: they are in the eye of the law property. In the eyes of their laws, we were their property. The Lord told us why: “And it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”

We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours, a land we are not familiar with. That is the servitude the Lord allowed because we forsook him.

So the slavery here was the curse on Israel for serving strange gods, not the obedience Colossians 3:22 teaches between Israelite servants and Israelite masters. They took the scripture and used it to hold us as property, but the Lord had already told us we would serve strangers.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Jeremiah said we would serve strangers in a land that is not ours. The Lamentations goes further: “Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Servants have ruled over us. This is Bible prophecy.

It happened in the time of Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America in the present day. It keeps happening over and over again. Why? Because we are the people of God. But this is the last time.

So the masters who took Colossians 3:22 and told us “Servants, obey in all things your masters” were themselves the servants ruling over Israel, just as the prophets lamented, with none to deliver us out of their hand.

precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Servants ruling over us happened with Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America present day. The Lord explains it to Ezra: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”.

A ring is a circular motion. You see this curse? It comes right back around, empire after empire, and it keeps happening because we are the people of God. But this is the last time. All praise to the Most High.

So the slavery in America where Colossians 3:22 was used against us is one more turn of that ring of judgment on Israel. It was not the Lord making the white man our rightful master; it was his judgment coming back around on his own people, and it ends with this last time.

They looked at us as their property: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
We were their property, and they still view us as that. They may have said we were equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

Nehemiah prayed it: “And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”. This is happening because we sinned against our God. “also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property, at their pleasure.

Their own book says it plainly: they are in the eye of the law property over which there is an absolute control; and by law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they don't want us to know the truth of the Bible, that servants obey your masters isn't talking about them. They want to keep us docile and uneducated.

precepts.text: He had power to give life unto the image of the beast: that false image of Christ. As many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. If our people did not agree, they were killed. Our people knew it was not true, but they did not want to die, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But it is a new generation on the earth, and we are not accepting the lies any more.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Their book says we may, according to the power lodged in our hands, forbid religious meetings, and no independent churches were allowed, so we depended on them alone. It went on during the Inquisition too, when they changed Christianity into the all-inclusive Catholic system and went around killing us, the real Jews, tearing up our safe houses and taking our book. The same thing is going to happen again, because now we know the truth. The only way the lie could hold strong was to destroy anybody who did not get down with it.

Revelation shows it: he “deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast”. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: that is the false image of Christ. “that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.”

If we did not agree to it, we were killed. Over time our people knew it wasn't true, but they didn't want to be killed, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But it's a new generation on the earth, and we aren't accepting the lies any more. We know we are the people, and we know what comes with the territory.

precepts.text: The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right. Even when we speak straight out of the Bible, they call it hate speech. The needy in that book is us.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The masters' book called us the most needy of any people in their country. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too: “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”

The needy in that book is us. The churl devised wicked devices with lying words: cherry-picking “Servants, obey in all things your masters”, writing directions for masters to bring slaves to their religion, forbidding our meetings and our reading.

And even when we speak straight out of the Bible, going precept upon precept, they call it hate speech. That is the needy speaking right and the churl answering with lying words to destroy the poor. So when Colossians 3:22 is read in context, it speaks of Israelite servants and Israelite masters, and the lying words that turned it against us are the churl's devices.

precepts.text: He that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons. The world calls it karma; the Bible says you shall receive for the wrong you have done.
precepts.point: Not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man, because Onias had a good report even among the other nations. The king was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger, he took away Andronicus his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city unto that very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, and there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Here is an easier verse to say what Job 34:11 says: “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.” You see how God gets down. In the world they call that karma. The Bible says if you do wrong, you shall receive for the wrong you have done.

There is no respect of persons. Jason was the high priest and it did not protect him: he undermined his own brother and was undermined by another. Andronicus was a man in authority, the king's deputy, and it did not protect him either. He came to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths, drew him out of the sanctuary and killed him, and the king took away his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city “unto that very place, where he had committed impiety against Onias, there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.” He received for the wrong he had done, in the very place he did it.

precepts.text: Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things. That is what minding earthly things means, and that is how it is with many Israelite camps today: everything becomes about the flesh instead of the godly things of the Lord.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.” Is Paul saying don’t get a job, don’t become an entrepreneur, don’t get married? No. He is talking about sexuality. The thought continues from the end of Colossians 2:23: “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.”

Philippians shows what minding the things on the earth looks like: “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When the flesh is your focus, your aim and your goal, you are minding earthly things.

That is how it is with many Israelite camps today: to hell with the godly things of the Lord, I want sex, sex and more sex, give it to me now. Men in those camps talk of two, three, four wives, and it becomes sexual immorality all over the place; those wicked spirits are back today. That is why Paul says to mortify the members upon the earth, “fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”: when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

precepts.text: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame. Paul is not saying to ignore what we need on earth; you need that to survive. Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage than delicate fare in another man's house: it is better to have your own place, no matter how humble, than to live sumptuously in somebody else's house. Be it little or much, hold thee contented. It is a miserable life to go from house to house: where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to ignore the things we need on earth when he said “not on things on the earth”? No. Paul was not running around contradicting the Bible; that is what the elders in these Israelite camps are doing.

“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You need that to survive. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” It is better to have your own place, brothers, no matter how messed up it is, because it is yours, than to live sumptuously in somebody else’s house.

“Be it little or much, hold thee contented, that thou hear not the reproach of thy house.” Whether you have a little or a lot, be content. “For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.”

So setting your affection on things above does not mean neglecting the needs of this life. It means not living to satisfy the flesh.

precepts.text: To all that are carried away captives: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them; take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that ye may be increased there, and not diminished. So Paul was not contradicting the Bible and telling anybody to reject work, education, marriage, or building. Increase even in Babylon.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Was Paul saying to reject the things on the earth, to hell with education, to hell with getting work? No. Jeremiah shows what the Lord told His people in captivity: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.”

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: get married and have children. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters”: pick good wives and good husbands for your children. “That ye may be increased there, and not diminished”: increased even there in Babylon.

So Paul was not contradicting the Bible. Seeking “those things which are above” does not mean rejecting work, education, marriage or building. It means putting to death the sins of the flesh, while still building houses, planting gardens and raising families even in captivity.

precepts.text: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, even as Christ forgave you. Some of us hold grudges like there is no tomorrow; imagine if Christ held on to grudges toward us. We would not be here. Forgiveness is something to pray for.
precepts.point: Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness”, the mercy Christ offers us, “humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”: longsuffering toward the brother who repents. “Forbearing one another”, as Christ forbears us, “and forgiving one another”.

Forgiving is something some of us need to pray for. Some can forgive nothing and hold on to grudges like there is no tomorrow. Imagine if Christ held on to grudges against us. We would not be here; we would be in hell with white Jesus, Islam and our sins. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ and his boundless mercy toward us.

“If any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” Christ does not put numbers out just to put them. Seventy times seven is 490, and Daniel's seventy weeks, 490 years from Persia to Christ, were determined “to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity” through the Messiah cut off for the children of Israel. We could not sacrifice in Babylon and Persia; we needed Christ, the complete perfection of mercy. He forgave us seventy times seven, so we forgive our brother the same, and we do not take him for granted.

precepts.text: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
precepts.point: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you: you want to seek pardon from the Lord while you hold hatred toward your brother? We read what that gets.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.

precepts.text: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord. Paul addressed this in almost all of his writings. What is fit in the Lord? As the Lord has designed. Can you truly say you are in the truth and you do not respect that man? You cannot, no matter how long you have been sitting here.
precepts.point: Sisters, if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The teaching from the teacher's own daughter: she comes running to the door, keeps her demeanor sweet, and can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you have to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel like he is everything he is supposed to be, and watch what happens. All sisters were taught to use the physical to get what they want; a righteous man needs your spirit to be right, and then you will see that Ephesians 5 man you desperately want.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
Paul addresses it in almost all of his writings: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.” What is fit in the Lord? As the Lord has designed. Can you truly say you are in the truth and not respect that man? You can't, no matter how long you have been sitting here.

We understand that, just as we men have residue from the world to beat, our wives do too; they are the weaker vessel, and Satan often comes through the woman to destroy the house. So we have to dwell with them according to knowledge and cast down every imagination with the scriptures. Sisters, your toughest plight in this truth is going to be honoring your husband. You tolerate all those folks at the job and listen to the boss; your husband is supposed to get many times more respect than him, and you never clock out. Even your anatomy tells you that you are to be submissive; it's the world telling you that you have options.

Reverence is deep respect for someone or something. Respect is deep admiration: esteem, regard, admiration, veneration, awe. That is what you are to have for your husband, even if he snores or limps when he walks, because you chose him. Imagine arguing with Christ: you can't even put that together in your mind. If he says park the car in that spot, it's law.

And if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The Deacon's daughter Mimi comes running to the door, Daddy!, and she can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you've got to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel he is everything he's supposed to be, and watch what happens. Get your spirit right, and you'll see that Ephesians 5 man you want.

precepts.text: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. Those are the durable riches Proverbs 8 speaks of.
precepts.point: Riches and honor are with me, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold. The riches we want are not money but the word dwelling in us richly.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

precepts.text: Lie not one to another. We must be men of honour so the world says surely this is a wise and understanding people. You cannot be in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; the word has to be far from your head for you to do it.
precepts.point: If the Lord exposes you through people volunteering your business unasked, he wants you to get right before you do it to the wrong person and the brothers find out at your funeral. You can hate the messenger or recognize the mercy, apologize, make amends, and walk in the spirit.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.” It is forbidden for us to lie one to another. We must be men of character, men of honour, because the world must look at us and say, surely this is a wise and understanding people. If you are lying, how is the world going to say that? They will say this is an evil-ass negro, and the truth gets evil spoken of, because the whole time you were doing it you had fringes on your clothes.

At no time did you look down at your fringes and say, damn, I can’t behave this way, I can’t do this to my brother, not even to people in the world. Why? Because you are not in the Bible. There is no way you are in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; it is an oxymoron. You just finished reading thou shalt not steal, I love that scripture, let me get my gun? It doesn’t go that way. The word has to be nowhere near your head for you to go do evil. That is why you stay in this Bible and give attendance to reading, continuously, so the word is in you.

A bishop “must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.” People in the world will lie on us, but they should never be able to back it up. In business in the world you must be twice as honourable, and you will get more jobs, because nobody likes a thief. Penny wise, pound foolish: make an extra penny now and lose the whole pound. Lie and steal, and you end up ducking people, circling the block, getting beaten over twenty dollars, and still owing the money. The devil convinced you it was okay to lie, then removed himself. Put off the old man and his deeds, and lie not one to another.

precepts.text: He that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done, and there is no respect of persons.
precepts.point: The traitor Jason slew his own countrymen to please the Greeks and died an exile.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Jason drove many out of their country and perished in a strange land; he cast out many unburied and had none to mourn for him. That is the law Paul states: “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.”

Negroes do evil and think there is not going to be a big payback. You are going to get it. It does not matter that Jason was an Israelite; there is no respect of persons. He slew his own citizens without mercy to please the Greeks, and he received shame for the reward of his treason.

And it was not only Jason. When the king heard of it, he thought Judea had revolted, took the city by force of arms, and there was “killing of young and old”, fourscore thousand destroyed in three days, and no fewer sold as slaves than slain. The Greeks were selling us as slaves long before the slave auctions we know today, and the ones among us who help the enemy against our own people will receive for the wrong they have done.

precepts.text: Servants, obey in all things your masters, in singleness of heart.
precepts.point: Onesimus was a servant who fled Philemon, and Paul sent him back as a brother.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh”. These are the same scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and that dumb black people use to reject the Bible. But it is not talking about chattel slavery. It is what was read in Leviticus 25 and Exodus: Israel, in a time of stability, still following the laws on selling yourself to work if you were poor or owed debts.

Leviticus says it: “And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then he departs, he and his children, back to his own family, because “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour”. Rigour is chattel slavery, and God forbade it over a brother.

Colossians says the same: “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants, hired servants.

Exodus 21 shows the master: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” If his master gave him a wife and she bore children, he could say, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”. Why would he say, I love my master? Because the brother treated him real good. That is what “Servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about.

precepts.text: Notice the admonition; nothing in it says soft or not firm. Provoking them to wrath is what sends them into the world, so build the foundation while they are young.
precepts.point: Fathers provoke not your children to anger. They see the instability, then watch you teach boldly in the streets and ask why you are not like that at home.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: Mortify therefore your members, fornication, uncleanness; for which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: For which things’ sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience”.

Uncleanness brings the wrath of God on the children of disobedience, and nothing that defileth enters the kingdom. Egypt was a nation of uncleanness that did not keep the covenant of circumcision; Israel is not to do after the doings of Egypt, and Moses' uncircumcised son brought the Lord to the inn to kill him.

precepts.text: Teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord; the command is spiritual songs, sung to the Most High.
precepts.point: The songs we make and listen to, now that we know the truth, should be spiritual songs; the psalms were the jams of that day, and every one of them is deep, teaching who the daughter of Babylon is, the crafty counsel taken against us, and that the law was given to Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.” The command is spiritual songs, sung to the Most High.

The songs we make and listen to, now that we know the truth, should be spiritual songs. The psalms were the jams of that day, and every one of them is deep, teaching who the daughter of Babylon is, the crafty counsel taken against us, and that the law was given to Israel.

precepts.text: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily as to the Lord and not unto men.
precepts.point: This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

precepts.why:
“And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men”. That is Hezekiah: “in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.”

This is the charge on every one of us. Do the work with everything you have, as unto the Lord, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow.

precepts.text: Mortify your members, fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness which is idolatry, for which the wrath of God comes on the disobedient.
precepts.point: David kept the Most High's judgments and statutes before him and kept himself from his iniquity. Iniquity is sin.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Keeping yourself from your iniquity means putting sin to death: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”.

Mortify your members: fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry. These are the things the wrath of God comes on the disobedient for.

David says, “I kept myself from mine iniquity.” Iniquity is sin, and this is the list to keep yourself from. That is the cleanness of hands the Lord recompenses.

precepts.text: And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
precepts.point: Everything from verse 38 down is charity, and charity is the bond of perfectness.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Everything from verse 38 down, resisting not evil, giving to him that asketh, loving your enemies and praying for them that persecute you, is charity. Paul says, “And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.”

Charity is the bond of perfectness. So when Christ closes with “Be ye therefore perfect”, the perfectness is bound up in the charity he has just taught, together with a heart that walks in the statutes and keeps the commandments.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” Endeavor means by any means necessary. Do whatever it takes to keep unity. “There is one body, and one Spirit”. That one body is Christ. One spirit. “One Lord, one faith, one baptism”. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. “One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

“But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.” We might not serve the same purpose, but we come together perfectly bound under Christ. He's the only one who can bring the southern and northern kingdoms together. The Bible and Christ's spirit can bring a thousand black men and a thousand Hispanics together without one fight. No other book can do that.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

Book read in class, on the Jewish diaspora: in spite of attempts to show that the Jews in the western diaspora knew Hebrew, it is common knowledge that basically they knew only Greek. The Jews of the west knew neither Hebrew nor Aramaic, and their religious lives, including the reading of the Torah and prayer, were conducted solely in Greek. The Torah was translated into Greek in the third century BCE. The sages recognized that there were entire diaspora communities that spoke only Greek, and provided a translation of scripture for the Greek-speaking communities. Rabbinic literature almost totally ignores the vast western diaspora that existed at that time, which is particularly noticeable compared with the relatively large number of places in this diaspora mentioned in chapter 2 of Acts, in the chapters describing the journeys of Paul, and in the Pauline epistles, which give a comprehensive picture of the geography of the western Jewish Greek-speaking diaspora in the first century.
